mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes SLS AMG Black Series engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M159.974 engine for the SLS AMG Black Series costs £26,000-£41,000 supply-only. Fitting adds £2,000-£3,500 depending on complexity - AMG V8 and dry sump work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of bearing wear on a Mercedes SLS AMG Black Series?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oil analysis showing elevated bearing metals, bearing knock, or low oil pressure warnings are the classic warning signs on the M159.974 engine. The Black Series' extreme output and track-focused calibration make bearing wear the most critical issue.

mainEntity.name: What causes oil pressure loss on a Mercedes SLS AMG Black Series?

acceptedAnswer.text: The multi-stage dry sump scavenge pump can suffer seal degradation and bearing wear under sustained lateral G-forces on track, reducing oil pressure to critical components. This is a critical failure that can destroy crank and rod bearings at speed.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes SLS AMG Black Series engine (M159.974) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M159.974 is a hand-built masterpiece - the most powerful naturally aspirated V8 ever produced by AMG. However, its track-focused design creates unique challenges. High-RPM bearing wear, crankshaft bearing fatigue, and piston ring wear are the most critical issues. With regular maintenance and proactive attention to known issues, the engine is fundamentally strong.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes SLS AMG Black Series engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M159.974 engines routinely reach 80,000-100,000 miles before major work, but track-used examples may require bearing attention from 40,000 miles. Regular oil analysis is essential for track-used Black Series examples.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes SLS AMG Black Series?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the Black Series is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M159.974 costs £26,000-£41,000 - far less than the £200,000-£350,000+ value of a clean Black Series. Investment-grade documentation, dyno certification, and unlimited warranty preserve provenance while restoring performance.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes SLS AMG Black Series - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The SLS AMG Black Series launched in 2013 as the ultimate track-focused variant of the SLS AMG range, powered by the hand-built M159.974 6.2-litre naturally aspirated V8 - the most powerful naturally aspirated V8 ever produced by AMG. With 591hp and 650Nm of torque, the Black Series represented the pinnacle of AMG's naturally aspirated V8 engineering, featuring motorsport-derived components, dry sump lubrication, and an aggressive track-focused calibration. Only a limited number were produced, making the Black Series one of the most sought-after AMG models ever built.

milestones.description: M159.974, 6.2L naturally aspirated V8, 591hp @ 7,400rpm, 650Nm torque (SLS AMG Black Series launch)

End of SLS AMG production; Black Series becomes a collector's icon

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes SLS AMG Black Series Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The SLS AMG Black Series M159.974 is the most powerful naturally aspirated V8 ever produced by AMG - a hand-built masterpiece with motorsport-derived components. However, its track-focused design and extreme output create unique challenges. High-RPM bearing wear, crankshaft bearing fatigue, piston ring wear, and dry sump pressure loss are the most critical issues driving replacement enquiries. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty with dyno certification and provenance documentation.

problems.h4: M159.974 High-RPM Bearing Wear - The Black Series' Most Critical Weakness
problems.rootCause: Sustained high-RPM operation and aggressive track driving place extreme loads on the M159.974's bearings. The Black Series' 591hp output and 7,400rpm redline demand precision bearing clearances that can degrade under sustained track use. High-RPM bearing wear is the most critical issue for Black Series owners.
